﴿A bringer of good news and a warner﴾: That is, bringing good news to the people of faith and righteous deeds of success, and warning the deniers and disbelievers of loss.

﴿But most of them turn away﴾: That is, most of the polytheists of Makkah and the disbelievers of Quraysh turned away from listening to the Qur'an.

﴿So they do not hear﴾: That is, they do not hear with understanding and reflection, so that they might benefit from what they hear.

﴿In coverings﴾: That is, coverings; the plural of kinān, which is that in which a thing is kept and concealed.

﴿And in our ears is deafness﴾: That is, heaviness, so we do not hear well.

﴿And between us and you is a barrier﴾: That is, a hindrance and a partition between us, so we do not hear what you say nor see what you do.

3- A demonstration of the intensity of the hostility of the polytheists toward monotheism and those who call to it in every time and place.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 41, verses 6–8:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Say, "I am only a human being like you."﴾ That is: I am not an angel; I am only a human being like you, from the descendants of Adam.

﴿It is revealed to me that your God is but one God.﴾ That is: God reveals to me that your God, i.e. your object of worship, O people, is one God, having no second and no more than one.

﴿So take the right course toward Him﴾: that is, devote your worship sincerely to Him alone, to the exclusion of anything else.

﴿And seek His forgiveness﴾: that is, ask Him to forgive your sins that were committed before going straight, namely polytheism and acts of disobedience.

﴿And woe to the polytheists﴾: that is, a severe punishment will befall them for angering the Lord by opposing Him with false deities.

﴿Who do not give zakah﴾: that is, the zakah of their wealth and the purification of their souls with that which cleanses them from the filth of polytheism and disobedience.

﴿For them is a reward uninterrupted﴾: that is, the reward of the Hereafter, which is Paradise and its bliss, which never ends in any way; this is "an unfailing reward."

Meaning of the verses:

After that dispute which the polytheists maintained in defense of idolatry and the ignorance of the Jahiliyyah, the Exalted commanded His Messenger to say to them: "I am only a human being like you in my humanity; I have never claimed otherwise, so I have not said that I am an angel. However, I am superior to you in one thing: it is revealed to me from my Lord. What is revealed to me is that your God is the true God, one, with no partner in His lordship or in His divinity. Accordingly, cast off those idols, take the right course toward Him, the Exalted, by sincerely devoting worship to Him and turning your faces to Him, and seek His forgiveness for the effects of the sin that preceded going straight in faith and monotheism."

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And woe to the polytheists﴾ informs that woe, which is the bitter punishment (since among the meanings of woe is the pus and putrid matter of the people of the Fire and what flows from their bodies and private parts), is for the polytheists who associate others with their Lord and who do not give the zakah of their wealth, and who, in the Hereafter, are disbelievers, that is, they do not believe in the Resurrection and recompense. Therefore they neither abandon evil nor do good, except a little and rarely, and the rare has no ruling.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds﴾: that is, those who believed in God, His promise, His threat, and His law, and did righteous deeds by performing the obligatory duties and much of the voluntary acts of worship, after avoiding polytheism, major sins, and wrongdoings; these have an unfailing reward in return for their faith and good deeds. The reward is the thawab (recompense), and what is meant by it is Paradise, since its bliss never ends for whoever attains it and succeeds in it under any circumstances.

Guidance of the verses:

1- Affirmation of prophethood and monotheism.

2- The obligation of going straight upon the law of God.

3- The obligation of seeking forgiveness for every sin, whether small or great.

4- The obligation of zakah on wealth, and the obligation of purifying souls through faith and good deeds.

Explanation of the words:

*Fa-in a'radu* ("But if they turn away"): i.e., the disbelievers of Quraysh turn away from faith and monotheism after this detailed clarification.

*Min bayni aydihim wa min khalfihim* ("from before them and from behind them"): i.e., their messengers came to them presenting the call to truth from their front and from their back.

*Law sha'a rabbuna la-anzala mala'ikatan* ("If our Lord had willed, He would have sent down angels"): i.e., in place of you, O messengers, who are human.

*Bi-ghayri al-haqq* ("without right"): i.e., without Allah having permitted them that haughtiness, arrogance and tyranny.

*Rihan sarsaran* ("a furious wind"): i.e., a wind with a sound heard as a roaring, together with extreme cold.

*Fi ayyamin nahsatin* ("on days of ill omen"): i.e., days inauspicious for them, after which they never prospered.

*Wa la-adhabu al-akhirati akhza* ("and the punishment of the Hereafter is more humiliating"): i.e., more severe in disgrace than the punishment of this world.

*Fa-astahabu al-'amá 'ala al-huda* ("They preferred blindness over guidance"): i.e., they preferred disbelief over faith, since disbelief is darkness and faith is light.

*Alladhina amanu wa kanu yattaqun* ("those who believed and used to be God-fearing"): i.e., those who avoided shirk and sins.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to seek the guidance of Quraysh, and Allah the Exalted says: *"But if they turn away"* after that clarification presented to them in the preceding verses, which made clear Allah's power, knowledge and wisdom, and what necessitates faith in His meeting and His oneness. So say to them: *"I have warned you of a thunderbolt,"* i.e., I have frightened you that a thunderbolt will descend upon you if you persist in your turning away, like the thunderbolt of 'Ad and Thamud, i.e., a destructive punishment like that with which Allah destroyed 'Ad and Thamud.

His saying: *"When the messengers came to them"*, namely Hud and Salih, *"from before them and from behind them"* is a metaphor that the messenger conveyed Allah's call to them to faith and monotheism with exceptional care, coming to them from their front and from their back calling them, saying to them: "Do not worship anything but Allah, for He is the true God, and whatever else is false." Their answer to them was: "We will not believe you and we will not accept from you. If Allah had willed, what you say to us He would have sent down to us through angels calling us to it, not sending someone like you from among mankind." And finally they said to them: "Indeed, we disbelieve in what you have been sent with," so the messengers despaired of their acceptance. This is what the first verse [13] and the second [14] indicate.

In the third verse [15], Allah explains the state of each of the two peoples separately. He says: *"As for 'Ad"*, i.e., the people of Hud, *"they were arrogant in the land without right"*, so the arrogance arising from material strength led them to reject the call of Hud, peace be upon him, and they said much against him and his message. This has passed in Surah Hud, and what is summarized here comes in detail in Surah al-Ahqaf. His saying *"without right"* means that their arrogance had no justification, first because of their weakness before the power of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and second because Allah the Exalted had not permitted them to be arrogant, so it is without right. His saying: *"And they said: 'Who is mightier than us in strength?'"* This was from them an explicit challenge and clear haughtiness and insolence. Therefore Allah challenged them with strength, saying, the Mighty and Majestic: *"Did they not see that Allah, who created them, is mightier than them in strength?"* i.e., were they blind and did they not see that Allah who created them is certainly mightier than them in strength, since every strength they have has its source in Allah, who created them and bestowed strength upon them. Their strength is not inherent but bestowed, for one of them is created unable to repel even the least thing from himself. His saying: *"And they used to deny Our signs"* records against them the greatest sin, which is their denial of the signs of Allah that the messenger Hud, peace be upon him, brought, just as Quraysh denied the signs of Allah. His saying, the Exalted: *"So We sent upon them"*, i.e., as soon as their disbelief was confirmed by their denial of Allah's signs, Allah the Exalted sent upon them *"a furious wind"*, i.e., cold, with a disturbing sound, which lasted seven nights and eight days, and it left none of them remaining. These were *"days of ill omen"* for them, inauspicious. Allah the Exalted said: *"That We might make them taste the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world."* i.e., We sent it upon them so that We might make them taste the punishment of humiliation in the life of this world.

They slaughtered the she-camel and intended to kill Salih, so the thunderbolt of humiliating punishment seized them, and that was on Saturday morning. A cry seized them by which their hearts were torn from their bodies, the earth quaked beneath them, and they were destroyed to the last one, *"because of what they used to earn"* of shirk, wrongdoing, disbelief and obstinacy. Allah saved Salih and those who were with him of the believers, *"those who believed and used to be God-fearing,"* who avoided shirk and sins, and they were four thousand believing men and women. This is the meaning of His saying at the conclusion of the account: *"And We saved those who believed and used to be God-fearing."*

Guidance from the verses:

1. Warning against turning away from answering the call of truth, and persisting in rebellion and disobedience.

2. Affirmation of monotheism, that there is no god but Allah.

3. The call of the messengers is one: commanding disbelief in false deities, and faith in Allah and worship of Him alone according to what He has legislated for mankind in acts of worship.

4. Condemnation of arrogance, and that it is the cause of disbelief and disobedience.

5. No calamity except for a sin: "because of what they earned," i.e., of sins.

6. Faith and piety are the path to salvation from punishment in this world and the Hereafter, and they are the two pillars of walayah, the allegiance of Allah, based on His saying: "Verily, the friends of Allah, no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve, those who believed and used to be God-fearing."

"Ardakum" (it destroyed you): i.e., it ruined you.

"Fa-in yasbiru fa-n-naru mathwan lahum" (So if they endure, the Fire is their abode): i.e., if they endure the punishment, then the Fire is their abode, that is, their dwelling place.

"Wa in yasta'tibu" (And if they seek to be pleased): i.e., if they seek 'utba, which is pleasure, "fa-la hum mina al-mu'tabin" (they will not be granted it): i.e., He will not be pleased with them; this is their condition forever.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues with the call to the Quraysh to the fundamentals of religion: monotheism, prophethood, resurrection and recompense. Within this context there is a presentation of one of the scenes of the Day of Resurrection, a vivid and wonderful scene presented before them.

The Exalted says: "And [mention] the Day when the enemies of Allah will be gathered to the Fire" (﴿ويَوْمَ يُحْشَرُ أعْدَآءُ ٱللَّهِ إلى ٱلنّارِ﴾), i.e., remind them of the day when the enemies of Allah, those who disbelieved in Him, did not believe and did not fear Him, will be gathered to the Fire. "So they are held back" (﴿فهم يوزعون﴾): their first ones are held back so that their last ones catch up, and they are driven together, some with others. "Until, when they reach it" (﴿حتى إذا ما جاءوها﴾), i.e., they arrive at it, and they claim that they are wronged and begin to disavow their sins, and they say that they will not accept a witness other than themselves. So Allah commands their hearing, their sight and their skins, and they bear witness against them "for what they used to do," and this is His saying: "Their hearing and their sight and their skins will testify against them as to what they used to do" (﴿شَهِدَ عَلَيْهِمْ سَمْعُهُمْ وأَبْصارُهُمْ وجُلُودُهُم بِما كانُواْ يَعْمَلُونَ﴾). Here they turn to their skins, blaming them and reproaching them, as He informed of in His saying: they said to their skins, "Why did you testify against us?" (﴿لِمَ شَهِدتُّمْ عَلَيْنا﴾). So the One able to do all this is able to make us speak and to make speak anything He wills to make speak. And His saying: "And you did not hide yourselves [so as to prevent] your hearing or your sight or your skins from bearing witness against you" (﴿وما كُنتُمْ تَسْتَتِرُونَ أن يَشْهَدَ عَلَيْكُمْ سَمْعُكُمْ ولا أبْصارُكُمْ ولا جُلُودُكُمْ﴾), i.e., you did not conceal yourselves so as to abandon the prohibitions of Allah; rather you were openly doing that because you did not believe in resurrection and recompense. "That was your assumption which you assumed about your Lord" (﴿وذَلِكُمْ ظَنُّكُمُ ٱلَّذِي ظَنَنتُم بِرَبِّكُمْ﴾), and it is an evil assumption. "It ruined you" (﴿أرْداكُمْ﴾), i.e., it destroyed you. "So you became among the losers" (﴿فَأَصْبَحْتُمْ مِّنَ ٱلُخاسِرِينَ﴾), those who lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection, and this is manifest loss. And His saying in the last verse of this context [24]: "So if they endure, the Fire is their abode" (﴿فإن يصبروا فالنار مثوى لهم﴾), i.e., the enemies of Allah, against whom their hearing, sight and skins have borne witness: the Fire is their abode, i.e., their dwelling place, from which they will never come out. Thus they are, in either case, in the worst state of the people of the Fire, and we seek refuge in Allah, Exalted is He.

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Affirmation of the creed of resurrection and recompense through a detailed presentation of the condition of the people of the Fire within it.

2- Warning against committing indecencies and grave sins, for a person's limbs bear witness against him.

3- Warning against evil assumptions about Allah Exalted, including that a person assumes that Allah does not see what he commits, or does not know it, or does not call him to account or recompense him.

The noble context continues with the call to the disbelievers of the Quraysh who turned away. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We appointed for them⦆ — that is, We sent to them companions from the devils. This came after they insisted upon falsehood and evil, and became so corrupt that it made it easy for the wicked jinn to associate with them. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 41, verses 33–36:

Explanation of the words:

"And who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah": that is, no one is better in speech than him, meaning than one who calls to the Oneness of Allah and obedience to Him.

"And does righteous deeds and says, 'Indeed, I am of the Muslims'": "And does righteous deeds" is also a condition; "And says, 'Indeed, I am of the Muslims'" is a third condition.

"Good and evil are not equal": that is, a good deed is not like an evil deed, nor is an evil deed like a good deed.

"Repel [evil] with that which is better": that is, repel evil, O believer, with the quality that is better, such as repelling anger with contentment and severance with keeping ties.

"As if he were a close friend": that is, as if he were a close, loving friend to you when you do that.

"But none is granted it except those who are patient": that is, none is given this quality which is better.

"Except one of great fortune": that is, great reward and abundant recompense, this in the Hereafter; as for this world, it is good character and perfection.

"And if there comes to you from Satan an evocation": that is, if Satan whispers to you to abandon good or to do evil.

"Then seek refuge in Allah": that is, then seek protection in Allah, saying, "I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan."

"Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing": that is, He, exalted is He, is the All-Hearing of the speech of His servants, the All-Knowing of what afflicts them and befalls them.

Meaning of the verses:

When Allah mentioned the glad tidings for the people of faith and righteous deeds, He here mentioned a second glad tiding for them as well, saying: "And who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah, does righteous deeds, and says, 'Indeed, I am of the Muslims'" (41:33). These are three conditions. The first: his calling to Allah, that He be worshipped and obeyed, not disobeyed, remembered and not forgotten, and thanked and not disbelieved. The second: "and does righteous deeds," so he performs the obligations and avoids the prohibitions. The third: he takes pride in Islam, glorying in it, and says, "Indeed, I am of the Muslims." So there is no one better in speech than this one whose conditions have been mentioned in full. This includes, first, the messengers; second, the scholars; third, the fighters in the cause of Allah; fourth, the muezzins; and fifth, the callers, the guided and the guiding. This is what the first verse [33] indicates.

And His saying, exalted is He: "Good and evil are not equal" (41:34). This is a divine affirmation that must be known: that good is not equal to evil, and evil is not equal to good. Faith is not equated with disbelief, piety is not equated with wickedness, and justice is not equated with injustice.

Just as the kinds of good deeds are not equal, the kinds of evil deeds are not equal either; rather they differ in merit. The fast of Ramadan is not equal to voluntary fasting in Rajab or Muharram, and the evil of killing a believer is not equal to insulting or striking him. And His saying: "Repel [evil] with that which is better" (41:34): that is, O our Messenger, after you have come to know that good and evil are not equal, repel evil with the quality that is better than other qualities. Then the one between whom and you there is enmity will turn into one who is dutiful to you, respectful of you, and welcoming to you, as if he were a cousin who loves and respects you. Since this quality, repelling with what is better, can only be attained by those of noble character and complete, honorable souls, Allah said: "But none is granted it" (41:35), that is, none is given this quality, "except those who are patient." So patience became one of their characteristics. "And none is granted it except one of great fortune" (41:35) in character and perfection of soul in this world, and in the great reward, which is Paradise, in the Hereafter.

And His saying: "And if there comes to you from Satan an evocation, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing" (41:36). The Lord, exalted is He, guides His servant and Messenger, and every individual of his community: if an evocation from Satan comes to him, by whispering to him to do evil or to abandon good, or if an evil thought occurs to him, he should turn to Allah, exalted is He, seeking His protection. For Allah, exalted is He, is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing. Seeking refuge in Him from Satan protects the servant and shields him from the whisperings of Satan and the evil thoughts he casts into the soul. Praise and grace are due to Allah for this divine guidance, which none of His servants can dispense with.

From the guidance of the verses:

2- The virtue of Islam, taking pride in it and sincerely glorying in it.

3- Affirmation that good is not equal to evil, and that good deeds vary in merit and evil deeds vary in merit.

4- The obligation for a Muslim brother to repel evil with good in speech and deed.

5- The virtue of the servant who perfects himself in soul and character, so that he repels evil with good.

6- The obligation to seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan when he whispers or casts an evil thought, for none can protect from him or guard against him except Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.

**Explanation of the words:**

*"And among His signs"*: that is, among the signs that point to the Lord, the Exalted, being the one true God.

*"And they do not tire"*: that is, they do not grow weary of His worship or become exhausted.

*"You see the earth lifeless"*: that is, dry and barren, with no plants and no life in it.

*"It stirs and swells"*: that is, it moves, swells, and plants appear in it.

His words, the Exalted, *"And among His signs"*: that is, among His many signs that point to His existence, power, knowledge and wisdom, and that call for belief in Him, His worship and His oneness (tawhid), are *"the night and the day"*, their alternation, and the regular order between them, so that the night does not overtake the day. Likewise the sun and the moon: He created them and set them in their orbits with extraordinary precision and exact measure. Therefore, O people, *"do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon,"* for they are both created beings among the creatures. Rather, *"prostrate to their Creator, if it is Him you worship"*, as you claim. Then He, the Exalted, said to His Messenger: *"If they refuse to respond to you and to listen to what I have said to them, out of arrogance, then know that those who are with your Lord,"* namely the angels, *"glorify Him night and day, and they do not tire of that or grow weary."*

His words, *"Indeed, He who revived it after its death is the one who will revive the dead,"* for He, the Exalted, is capable of doing everything He wills; nothing can prevent Him or overpower Him. And how could it not be so, when, if He wills a thing, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.

1- Establishing tawhid (the oneness of God) through decisive proofs that make worship due to Him alone and to no other of His creatures.

Water will then come down from the sky, and people will live and grow from the coccyx (ajb al-dhanab), as plants grow from the seed that lies hidden in the soil.

5- Establishing that God has power over everything He wills. This attribute belongs to Him alone, and it calls for His worship and obedience after belief in Him and devotion to Him alone.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 41, verses 40–42:

Explanation of the words:

Yulhiduna fi ayatina (﴿those who distort Our signs﴾): i.e., they dispute concerning them and incline them away from their true meaning, interpreting them in ways other than their intended sense, in order to nullify a truth or establish a falsehood.

La yakhfawna 'alayna (﴿are not hidden from Us﴾): i.e., they are exposed before Us, and We will seize them as recompense for their distortion.

Afaman yati amanan yawm al-qiyamah (﴿Is one who is cast into the Fire better, or one who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection?﴾): i.e., indeed, the one who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection is better than the one who is thrown into the Fire.

I'malu ma shi'tum (﴿Do what you will﴾): this is a threat to them for their distortion, not a permission for them to act as they wish.

Inna alladhina kafaru bi'l-dhikr (﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the Reminder﴾): i.e., they denied the Qur'an or distorted it, and thereby they disbelieved.

Wa innahu la-kitabun 'aziz (﴿And indeed it is a mighty Book﴾): i.e., the Qur'an is a mighty Book, impregnable, which none can add to or subtract from.

La ya'tihi al-batilu min bayni yadayh (﴿Falsehood cannot approach it from before it﴾): i.e., no devil among jinn or men can add anything to it, and this is the meaning of "from before it."

Wa la min khalfih (﴿nor from behind it﴾): i.e., no devil among jinn or men can diminish anything from it, and this is the meaning of "from behind it." Likewise, there is no earlier book that could diminish it, nor a later book that could abrogate it. It is entirely truth and sincerity, containing nothing that does not correspond to reality.

Meaning of the verses:

The Almighty, the Majestic, threatens those who distort the verses of His Book through alteration, substitution and change, warning that they are not hidden from Him, and that He will bring down His vengeance upon them unless they desist from their distortion.

As for His saying: "Is one who is cast into the Fire better, or one who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection?" — since no rational person would say that one cast into the Fire is better than one who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection, the cause of being cast into the Fire is disbelief, distortion and falsehood, so whoever wishes to be saved from the Fire should abandon these. Security on the Day of Resurrection from every fear, of the Fire and other things, is caused by faith and monotheism, so let him believe and affirm God Most High in His worship, and let him not distort His verses, if he wishes security on the Day of Resurrection, knowing that it is better than being cast into the Fire. This is a wondrous method of invitation (to faith) that the Noble Qur'an alone has adopted.

As for the saying of God Most High: ﴿Do what you will; indeed He is Seer of what you do﴾: this speech is directed at those who treat the legal rulings with contempt and make light of them. It is a threat to them, not a permission or allowance for them to do whatever falsehood, polytheism and evil they wish. What indicates the threat is His saying after it: "Indeed He is Seer of what you do."

Similarly, His saying: ﴿Indeed those who disbelieve in the Reminder﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿and indeed it is a mighty Book﴾, i.e., impregnable and unattainable, ﴿falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it﴾, by addition or subtraction, or alteration and change.

Since the purpose of this speech is threat, the consequence has been omitted, as it is too evident to mention, and expression may fall short of conveying it in its actual form. It may be understood as: "We will surely do to them such and such..."

As for His saying: ﴿A revelation from the All-Wise, the Praiseworthy﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, mighty in its perfection, its nobility and its inviolability, is a revelation from One who is All-Wise in His acts and all His dispositions, and Praiseworthy for this and for His other bounties, favours and blessings.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The prohibition of distorting the signs of God by inclining them away from their intended sense and taking them toward falsehood.

2- A severe threat to everyone who alters the signs of God or interprets them contrary to God's intended meaning.

3- Affirmation of the inviolability of the Qur'an and God's preservation of it, and that no deficiency or addition will enter it until God raises it to Himself, for from Him it began and to Him it returns.

So His saying: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own self, and whoever does evil, it is against himself﴾, the return of the evil upon its doer, is indeed a consolation for everyone who wishes to console himself and be patient.

1. Consoling the Messenger, that is, strengthening him to be patient and find solace, so that he continues his call to its end.

2. Clarifying the extent of the denial, obstinacy and denial that the polytheists displayed towards the Messenger.

3. The Qur'an is a remedy and healing for the people of faith, while for the people of disbelief it is the opposite, since they stand in contrast to the people of faith.

4. Clarifying Allah's way with earlier nations regarding their disputing over their prophets and what guidance and light those prophets brought them.

5. His saying: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own self, and whoever does evil, it is against himself﴾ has become a proverb among scholars.

6. The absolute negation of injustice from Allah.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 41, verse 49–51:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Lā yas'amu al-insānu min du'ā'i al-khayr﴾: i.e., he does not tire or grow weary of asking for wealth, health and well-being.

﴿Wa-in massahu al-sharru fa-ya'ūsun qanūt﴾: i.e., illness, poverty and other such things; so he despairs of God's mercy, a despair openly visible upon him.

﴿Min ba'di ḍarrā' massat-hu﴾: i.e., after a hardship that afflicted him and a trial that befell him.

﴿La-yaqūlanna hādhā lī﴾: i.e., I deserve this by my own effort and because of my own standing.

﴿Wa-mā aẓunnu al-sā'ata qā'imah﴾: i.e., he denies the resurrection and says: I do not think the Hour will come.

﴿In lī 'indahu lal-ḥusnā﴾: i.e., and even supposing what the messengers said about resurrection is true, I will have the Garden with God.

﴿A'raḍa wa-nā'a bi-jānibih﴾: i.e., he turns away from gratitude and turns aside with his side, strutting and swaggering in his gait.

﴿Fa-dhū du'ā'in 'arīḍ﴾: i.e., he is one who makes long, extensive supplication to his Lord: "O Lord! O Lord!"

The meaning of the verses:

He, exalted is He, informs about the disbelieving human being whose soul has not been purified and whose spirit has not been cleansed by faith and righteous deeds: he does not tire or grow weary of asking for good things—wealth, children, health and well-being—so he is never satisfied with such things in any state. And if evil touches him, such as harm, poverty or the like, he is despairing, desperate, with the traces of despair openly visible in his speech and in his whole condition. This is what the first verse [49] contains: ﴿Man does not tire of asking for good, but if evil touches him, he is despairing and desperate.﴾

As for the verse [50], God, exalted is He, also informs about the disbelieving human being: when God lets him taste mercy from Him—wealth, health, reunion of family, for example—after a hardship that afflicted him, such as illness, poverty or the like, he says, in his ignorance and foolishness: "This is mine," i.e., I deserve it through my wealth, effort, standing and knowledge. And when he is reminded of the Hour, so that he may be gentle or give charity, he says: "I do not think the Hour will be established, as you say." And even if it were established, supposing your saying is true, "I will have with Him," i.e., with God, "the best," i.e., the best state of wealth and other things, and a Garden, if it is as you say.

As for His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Then We will certainly inform those who disbelieved of what they did﴾, i.e., on the Day of Resurrection when they are brought before Us, ﴿and We will surely make them taste a severe punishment﴾, in which they will abide forever, never coming out of it.

As for His saying, exalted is He, in the last verse [51]: when We bestow blessings upon the human being—the blessing of wealth, children and health—he turns away from remembering Us and thanking Us, forsakes obedience to Us, and turns aside with his side, distant and swaggering, almost resembling the peacock in his gait. And when We take that from him and harm touches him—illness, poverty, hardship and trial—then he is "one of long, extensive supplication to Us: O Lord, O Lord, O Lord." This is not the first man who despairs and becomes desperate; that one is a disbeliever, while this one is a believer of weak faith, ignorant, having no discipline or character. How many of this kind of men there are among Muslims today—and we seek refuge in God, exalted is He. The first returns to the darkness of his own soul through disbelief, and this one returns to his poor upbringing, his bad character and the darkness of his ignorance.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Description of the state of the human being before faith and steadfastness, for he is the lowest of creatures in rank and the weakest in standing.

2- Affirmation of the doctrine of resurrection and recompense through mention of some of its events.

3- Condemnation of despair, desperation, arrogance, vanity, ingratitude for blessings, forgetting the Benefactor, and failing to give Him thanks.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 41, verses 52–54:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Say: Have you considered, if it is from Allah⌋: that is, inform me: if the Qur'an is from Allah, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said.

Then you disbelieved in it: that is, then you disbelieved in it after knowing that it is from Allah.

Who is more astray than one who is in extreme opposition?: that is, who would be more astray than you, while you are in far-reaching opposition? No one.

On the horizons and within themselves: that is, in the regions of the heavens and the earth, among the created beings and the secrets of their creation, and within themselves, among the subtleties of craftsmanship and the wonders and marvels of wisdom.

Until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth: that is, that the Qur'an is truly the speech of Allah and His revelation to His Messenger, and that Islam is true.

Unquestionably, they are in doubt about meeting their Lord: that is, in doubt about the final resurrection, when they will be presented before Allah, exalted is He.

Unquestionably, He encompasses all things: that is, in knowledge, power, might and dominion.

The meaning of the verses:

Allah commands His Messenger (ﷺ) to say to those who deny the divine revelation, which the noble Qur'an represents, and who said about it that it is poetry, magic and the fables of the ancients, that he should say to them, asking them: "Have you considered: that is, inform me, if the Qur'an which you denied is from Allah and you disbelieved in it, that is, denied it? Who would be more astray than you while you live in far-reaching opposition?" By God, no one would be more astray than you from the path of guidance. So why do you not return to your right sense, believe in the signs of your Lord, and thus be saved and prepare for yourselves?

Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿We will show them Our signs⌋ which indicate the truthfulness of Us and of Our Messenger in what We informed them of and called them to, of faith, monotheism, resurrection and recompense. This is in the horizons, that is, in the regions of the heavens and the earth, of what the days will reveal of the wonders of Allah's governance and the subtleties of His craftsmanship; and within themselves as well, that is, in their own selves, until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth. Among that is the conquest of towns and cities and the victory of Islam as the Qur'an reported; and the Battle of Badr and the conquest of Makkah are among that, and what has appeared until now of discoveries in the horizons and within the selves, which the Qur'an has alluded to, is even more wondrous than that. Consider His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And of all things We created pairs, that you may remember⌋ [adh-Dhariyat: 49]. The system of pairing that pervades every particle of the universe is strong evidence of the truthfulness of the Qur'an, that it is the truth from Allah, and that Allah is the Truth, and the Hour is the Truth. And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Is it not sufficient concerning your Lord that He is, over all things, a Witness?⌋ This is a rebuke to these deniers, informing them that the testimony of Allah is sufficient for the truthfulness of Muhammad and what he brought, for it is Allah who informs of that and commands belief in him. So how can they demand signs for the truthfulness of the Qur'an and of the one to whom it was sent, when Allah is the One who sent the Messenger and sent down the Book? And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Unquestionably, they are in doubt about meeting their Lord⌋ is an announcement from Him, Exalted, of what the people are upon of doubt regarding resurrection and recompense, and this is what caused them much kinds of evil and corruption.

And His saying: ﴿Unquestionably, He encompasses all things⌋ in knowledge, power, might and dominion. So what He informed them of about themselves, and what He will recompense them with of punishment if they persist in their disbelief, is from His power and His might. Unquestionably, let whoever is afflicted with doubt about resurrection fear Allah, for all the signs indicate its certainty and its occurrence at its appointed time.

Guidance of the verses:

Among the guidance of the verses:

1- Condemnation of disbelief in the Qur'an and denial of the guidance and light it contains.

2- None is more astray than one who denies the Qur'an, for he lives in a opposition and dissension with no greater remoteness.

3- The truthfulness of Allah's promise, for He showed the polytheists and others His signs which indicate His oneness, the soundness of His religion and the truthfulness of His reports, which the people who cannot be counted in number believed in.

4- Every discovery that has appeared and will appear is included by the Qur'an in this verse: "We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves."

5- An indication that Islam will be known to be sound, and all mankind will adopt it at some point in time.

6- Affirmation of resurrection and recompense, and of the manifestations of Allah's power that establish it.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 41, verses 52–54:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Say: Have you considered, if it is from Allah⌋: that is, inform me: if the Qur'an is from Allah, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said.

Then you disbelieved in it: that is, then you disbelieved in it after knowing that it is from Allah.

Who is more astray than one who is in extreme opposition?: that is, who would be more astray than you, while you are in far-reaching opposition? No one.

On the horizons and within themselves: that is, in the regions of the heavens and the earth, among the created beings and the secrets of their creation, and within themselves, among the subtleties of craftsmanship and the wonders and marvels of wisdom.

Until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth: that is, that the Qur'an is truly the speech of Allah and His revelation to His Messenger, and that Islam is true.

Unquestionably, they are in doubt about meeting their Lord: that is, in doubt about the final resurrection, when they will be presented before Allah, exalted is He.

Unquestionably, He encompasses all things: that is, in knowledge, power, might and dominion.

The meaning of the verses:

Allah commands His Messenger (ﷺ) to say to those who deny the divine revelation, which the noble Qur'an represents, and who said about it that it is poetry, magic and the fables of the ancients, that he should say to them, asking them: "Have you considered: that is, inform me, if the Qur'an which you denied is from Allah and you disbelieved in it, that is, denied it? Who would be more astray than you while you live in far-reaching opposition?" By God, no one would be more astray than you from the path of guidance. So why do you not return to your right sense, believe in the signs of your Lord, and thus be saved and prepare for yourselves?

Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿We will show them Our signs⌋ which indicate the truthfulness of Us and of Our Messenger in what We informed them of and called them to, of faith, monotheism, resurrection and recompense. This is in the horizons, that is, in the regions of the heavens and the earth, of what the days will reveal of the wonders of Allah's governance and the subtleties of His craftsmanship; and within themselves as well, that is, in their own selves, until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth. Among that is the conquest of towns and cities and the victory of Islam as the Qur'an reported; and the Battle of Badr and the conquest of Makkah are among that, and what has appeared until now of discoveries in the horizons and within the selves, which the Qur'an has alluded to, is even more wondrous than that. Consider His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And of all things We created pairs, that you may remember⌋ [adh-Dhariyat: 49]. The system of pairing that pervades every particle of the universe is strong evidence of the truthfulness of the Qur'an, that it is the truth from Allah, and that Allah is the Truth, and the Hour is the Truth. And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Is it not sufficient concerning your Lord that He is, over all things, a Witness?⌋ This is a rebuke to these deniers, informing them that the testimony of Allah is sufficient for the truthfulness of Muhammad and what he brought, for it is Allah who informs of that and commands belief in him. So how can they demand signs for the truthfulness of the Qur'an and of the one to whom it was sent, when Allah is the One who sent the Messenger and sent down the Book? And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Unquestionably, they are in doubt about meeting their Lord⌋ is an announcement from Him, Exalted, of what the people are upon of doubt regarding resurrection and recompense, and this is what caused them much kinds of evil and corruption.

And His saying: ﴿Unquestionably, He encompasses all things⌋ in knowledge, power, might and dominion. So what He informed them of about themselves, and what He will recompense them with of punishment if they persist in their disbelief, is from His power and His might. Unquestionably, let whoever is afflicted with doubt about resurrection fear Allah, for all the signs indicate its certainty and its occurrence at its appointed time.

Guidance of the verses:

Among the guidance of the verses:

1- Condemnation of disbelief in the Qur'an and denial of the guidance and light it contains.

2- None is more astray than one who denies the Qur'an, for he lives in a opposition and dissension with no greater remoteness.

3- The truthfulness of Allah's promise, for He showed the polytheists and others His signs which indicate His oneness, the soundness of His religion and the truthfulness of His reports, which the people who cannot be counted in number believed in.

4- Every discovery that has appeared and will appear is included by the Qur'an in this verse: "We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves."

5- An indication that Islam will be known to be sound, and all mankind will adopt it at some point in time.

6- Affirmation of resurrection and recompense, and of the manifestations of Allah's power that establish it.
